initial.reason: Monomer1 is a hydroquinone diglycidyl ether-type structure containing two epoxide rings (explicit C1OC1 and C2OC2 motifs) for crosslinking. Monomer2 is 4,4'-methylenedianiline (two aniline NH2 groups, i.e., NC reactive sites) providing at least two amine nucleophiles to cure the epoxides. The epoxy (monomer1) / amine (monomer2) pairing is highly compatible for thermoset formation. Aromatic, rigid cores in both monomers increase Tg toward the 150 °C target, while the difunctional nature (two epoxides, two amines) yields a moderate crosslink density consistent with an intermediate rubbery modulus (Er ≈ 75). Both SMILES are chemically plausible and synthetically accessible building blocks for an amine-cured epoxy TSMP.

This design increases reactive site density relative to the prior pair and improves compatibility (epoxy + multi-amine) to move Er toward the target while keeping a rigid aromatic epoxy to support a high Tg.
